the R2c scaffold is a remodeled Rv0233 scaffold.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new Mn/Fe cofactors has been found in a new scaffold.

the heterodinucleating R2c-like protein from C. trachomatis and Rv0233c from M. tuberculosis are both R2 homologs, but Rv0233 is a remodeled Rv0233 that is not a functional R2 protein but a ligand binding oxidase.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the R2 scaffold is highly flexible and can be remodeled to support a wide variety of biological functions.
Rv0233 is not a ribonucleotide-reductase R2 homologue, as previously proposed, but a ligand-binding Mn- and Fe-dependent oxidase that may play a role in virulence of M. tuberculosis.

the R2 protein family, which includes the prototype of ribonucleoside reductase and a large group of bacterial multicomponent oxidases, has a much larger functional repertoire than previously anticipated.
